title: docs(adr): ADR-0067 records the revert doors after #33805
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-steve"} -->
_Requested by **Steve** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9?thread=cmsg_01FdL1XeUyvVNxLreh3F4Qi9Ugitvur3Y1e4hZEA7aUAfG)_

Fixes #33850

Clause-②: no
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- 改了什么:只动 ADR-0067 一个文件,只追加、只加标记。Status 行追加一条 2026-11-15 的 Amended;文末新增一节 2026-11-15 Amendment;在 11-14 那节加了三个 ⚠️ 指针(「What the doors do」开头、「不裁决」第二条、「Recorded by」段后),另在 D3 第一条的旧括注后加一个。
- 为什么改:11-14 那节记录的是代码在 `ba35dfd7` 时的样子。PR #33805 和 PR #33979 合并后,撤销提交(revertCommit)会读五类行写入之后的故障,把条目放进 `failed[]` 并让 `success` 为 false;撤销提交记下每行被替换前的版本,所以「撤销这次撤销」能恢复;没有可恢复版本的条目会被点名而不是跳过。ADR 还在说旧行为。
- 风险与回滚:纯文档,不发布任何包,不改代码和测试。历史文字一字未改(两处被改的行都只是在行尾追加)。回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- 先看:`docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md` 文末新节的第一条和第三条(撤销读哪五类故障、哪些结果仍然不进 `failed[]`;第一轮的正文把这里写错了,后两轮改的都是这里);再看「What this replaces in the 2026-11-14 Amendment」清单;最后看 Status 行新增的那一条。
- 两分钟验证:`pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors && pnpm check:adr-index`,预期看到 3632 个锚点全部解析,以及「docs/adr/README.md is current」。
- 需要你做的:暂无。增量契约评审在 `570a7460` 上为 PASS(记录 6898997083),但留了一条 should-fix 和一条 nit;处理它们之后的 head `e6a8068b` 还欠一次增量契约评审,目前没有 PASS 记录指向这个 head。

## What changes

One file, `docs/adr/0067-commit-history-and-rollback-for-ai-authoring.md`, append and mark only (Prime Directive 13). No code, no test, no changeset.

1. **Status line.** A new `· **Amended** (2026-11-15, #33850 — …)` entry is appended after the 2026-11-14 one. The line still opens with `Accepted`, so the index reading does not move (`adr-index --report`: README current).
2. **New section at the end**, `## Amendment (2026-11-15, #33850)`. It records what the two revert doors do on `main`, read off the code at `fb79d47c`:
   - The five faults the revert reads after an item's row write put the item in `failed[]` with the row state, and `success` is false: the registry write-through's answer, any storage advisory, the projector's `success: false`, the heal's answered stop where a row was removed, and a later throw.
   - Which PR reads which. PR #33805 reads the storage advisory, the projector, the later throw and the registry's refusal of an `object`. The non-object write-through faults and the heal's answered stop came with PR #33979.
   - What still does not reach `failed[]`: registry heal outcomes that answer no stop, on either limb (an open list: among them the registry refusing to unregister a removed object, a package-scoped refusal of the baseline read, a degraded baseline read, a stored `object_extension` that cannot be registered again, and the heal of a view container's member views, whose answer is not kept), the mutation event, and the stored-expression fill.
   - The revert commit is written from the revert's own plan, not from `reverted[]`.
   - Each plan item records the version the row held before the revert, so reverting a revert restores on both limbs.
   - An item recorded as existing with no version to restore is named in `failed[]`, and nothing is written. Every revert commit recorded before PR #33805 has that shape.
   - The revert commit record is still best effort, and the `rollbackToPackageCommit` docblock now says so (the `[#33486]` sentence, quoted).
   - It lists each sentence of the 2026-11-14 Amendment it replaces, and says what still holds.
   - It decides nothing. Whether a revert should be atomic is still open, and so is whether a heal outcome that answers no stop should reach `failed[]`.
3. **Four in-place marks** (the old text stays as written):
   - a ⚠️ blockquote at the top of the 2026-11-14 "What the doors do" section;
   - a ⚠️ line under the second bullet of that amendment's "What this amendment does not decide";
   - a ⚠️ blockquote after that amendment's "Recorded by" paragraph;
   - a ⚠️ parenthetical appended to D3's first bullet, whose 2026-11-14 note says "reverting a revert commit restores nothing today".

TL;DR 3's parenthetical and D3's second-bullet parenthetical still hold, so they are not marked.

### Review round 1 (record 6898709078, FAIL on `36487820`)

- **M-1 (must-fix), fixed.** The section said two things still do not reach `failed[]`. There are three: the heal outcomes that answer no stop were missing. The section now lists the five faults the revert reads, and lists the heal outcomes beside the mutation event and the fill. The section title, the Status entry, the mark on "does not decide" and the first "What this replaces" entry now say "the faults the revert reads". The mark at the top of "What the doors do" says the 2026-11-14 account of the heal (not reported, item in `reverted[]`) is still true for those outcomes. Each outcome was checked against `protocol-registry-hydration.ts#restoreArtifactRegistryView` on `main`.
- **S-1, fixed.** The mark at the top of "What the doors do" now quotes the stale sentence, "A fault after an item's row write is not named there, and a skipped item is not named at all."
- **N-1, fixed.** The 2026-11-14 "Recorded by" paragraph has its own mark: two of its three points no longer hold, and the first still says more than the code.
- **N-2, fixed.** The function-local names and expression fragments are gone. The section describes behaviour in prose and anchors public symbols only (`revertCommit`, `rollbackToPackageCommit`, `restoreArtifactRegistryView`, `RegistryHealStop`, `RegistryWriteThroughRequest`).
- **N-3, fixed.** The heal's answered stop is attributed to PR #33979. The storage step is "any advisory" (a refused sync, or column changes that were not applied).
- **N-4, fixed.** "What this replaces" no longer retires the whole "An item can also be skipped" bullet. It names the replaced parts and says the parenthetical still holds for a revert commit recorded before PR #33805.
- **O-1 (ADR-0094), not touched.** It is outside this file surface, and the seat files it separately.

### Review round 2 (record 6898997083, PASS on `570a7460`, one should-fix and one nit open)

- **S-2 (should-fix), fixed.** The section no longer counts what still does not reach `failed[]`. The heal outcomes are an open list ("among them") on either limb. Two outcomes are added, each checked on `main`: for a removed `object_extension`, a stored extension that cannot be registered again is only logged at `warn` (`protocol-class-head.ts#resyncStoredObjectExtensions`); and the member views of a view container are healed by `protocol-registry-hydration.ts#reconcileViewExpansions`, which does not keep the heal's answer, on the soft-remove limb and, through the write-through of a restored container, on the restore limb.
- **N-5 (nit), fixed.** The Status entry says "still not reported" where it said "still only logged", because the degraded read logs nothing. The same change was made to the one sentence in the section that said a stop "stays on the log".
- **Body wording.** The 速读 no longer reads as if the review erred, and no longer counts the unread outcomes.

**Authoring tier.** The ADR text, in all three rounds, was written by an isolated os-dev subagent pinned to the model tier fable (CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER), because `docs/adr/**` requires that tier and the card thread is served below it.

## Tests

No test changes. A docs-only diff has nothing to ablate. The text cites the existing pin, `packages/metadata-protocol/src/protocol.revert-commit-honest-outcome.test.ts`, by its describe and it names; that suite was not run locally (the diff touches no package) and runs in CI.

## Acceptance notes

- The three facts on the card hold on `main`. Each was checked against the code at `fb79d47c`. Main has moved to `63db7240` since; the files the section reads (`protocol-package-commits.ts`, `protocol-registry-hydration.ts`, `protocol-class-head.ts`, `protocol.ts`, `protocol-package-commit-record.ts`, the pin test) are unchanged across that range.
- The card attributes the whole change to PR #33805. One part is not from that PR: the non-object registry faults and the heal's answered stop landed in PR #33979 (`0bbb211f`, for #33851). The section names both PRs and says which did what.
- Read, not filed: the comment above the revert's plan in `revertCommit` says "one item per row the walk changed", but the soft-remove limb also adds a plan item when it found no row to remove. The ADR section states what the code does. class: observation, carrier: none.
- Append-only proof: against `origin/main` the diff has two removed lines, and each is a prefix of the line that replaces it (the Status line and D3's first bullet). Everything else is insertion: +209 / -2.

## Verification

All readings are on head `e6a8068b` (round 2's fix commit on top of a merge of `origin/main` at `63db7240`). Round 2 handled S-2 and N-5. `git diff --name-only origin/main...HEAD` lists the ADR file only.

The one build the list needs, `pnpm turbo run build --filter='@objectstack/lint...' --concurrency=2`, ran under the verify lock: `VERDICT command-exit 0 · held the lock 1s` (a cache replay of round 0's 86 s build).

<summary>ADR registry, status line and anchors</summary>

- `pnpm check:adr-index` (exit 0): "adr-index --report: OK — docs/adr/README.md is current, every record parsed, self-test 60 assertions green." The new Status entry needs no README regeneration, so the file surface stays at the one ADR.
- `pnpm check:adr-symbol-anchors` (exit 0): "3632 anchors across 156 records resolve — 1057 symbol (1030 declaration, 27 literal), 2523 file-level, 52 cross-repo, 6 exempt, 73 continuation. 0 line anchors survive". On the base tree `fb79d47c` the same gate read 3622 anchors, 1050 symbol, 2520 file-level, 72 continuation. The difference is this PR's anchors, all resolving.
- `pnpm check:adr-anchors` (exit 0). It is in the derived list above.
